facts: On 13 September 1993, on the White House lawn, Israel's prime minister Yitzhak Rabin and PLO chairman Yasser Arafat shook hands, with President Clinton. The Oslo Accords promised Palestinian self-government and a path to a final peace deal. In 1994 Rabin, Arafat and Shimon Peres shared the Nobel Peace Prize. In November 1995 an Israeli extremist assassinated Rabin. In 2005 Israel pulled its settlers and soldiers out of Gaza. In 2007 Hamas took control of the Gaza Strip.

lines.say: In September 1993, on the White House lawn, Israel's Yitzhak Rabin and the PLO's Yasser Arafat shook hands.
The Oslo Accords promised Palestinian self-government, and a path to a final peace deal.
A year later, Rabin, Arafat and Shimon Peres shared the Nobel Peace Prize.
But the deal had bitter enemies on both sides. In November 1995, an Israeli extremist assassinated Rabin.
In 2005, Israel pulled its settlers and soldiers out of Gaza.
Two years later, Hamas took control of the Strip.
